meta.mechanism: secretory phospholipase A2 (sPLA2) inhibitor (broad: groups IIA, V, X)
meta.indication: short-term (16-week) treatment after acute coronary syndrome to reduce recurrent cardiovascular events

n_randomized.quote: A double-blind, randomized, multicenter trial at 362 academic and community hospitals in Europe, Australia, New Zealand, India, and North America of 5145 patients randomized within 96 hours of presentation of an acute coronary syndrome (ACS) to either varespladib (n = 2572) or placebo (n = 2573)
n_randomized.note: Registry S3 lists enrollment 5189 (ACTUAL) - conflict, see open_questions. 5012 randomized at the time of the interim analysis.

median_followup.quote: Participants were randomized to receive varespladib (500 mg) or placebo daily for 16 weeks, in addition to atorvastatin and other established therapies.
median_followup.note: Median follow-up NOT FOUND; trial was terminated early so many patients had <16 weeks. Primary end point assessed at 16 weeks; six-month survival status also evaluated.

primary_endpoint.value: Composite of CV death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or unstable angina with evidence of ischemia requiring hospitalization at 16 weeks
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary efficacy measure was a composite of cardiovascular mortality, nonfatal myocardial infarction (MI), nonfatal stroke, or unstable angina with evidence of ischemia requiring hospitalization at 16 weeks.
primary_endpoint.note: Agreed with FDA under a Special Protocol Assessment (S4, S6).

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Age >=40, hospitalized with ACS (UA, NSTEMI or STEMI), randomized within 96 hours of presentation; on atorvastatin background; high-risk features required
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Patients aged 40 years or older hospitalized with an ACS who provided written, informed consent were eligible to participate
inclusion_key_criteria.note: JAMA full text via WebFetch. Also: 'Patients were randomized within 96 hours of presentation of the index event in a 1:1 ratio.' Press release S4: high-risk = 'previous cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or metabolic syndrome'. 'Patients were not selected for randomization on the basis of their underlying sPLA2 concentration or activity.'

planned_events.quote: The trial was designed to enroll 6500 patients, assuming an 8.5% primary end point event rate in the placebo group, with 80% power to detect a 25% reduction in the relative risk of the varespladib group, necessitating the adjudication of 385 primary end point events.
planned_events.note: Public before readout: Anthera press release 2011-04-18 (S4): 'Enrollment in VISTA-16 will be stopped after a minimum of 385 primary endpoint events have occurred.'

assumed_rrr.quote: The trial was designed to enroll 6500 patients, assuming an 8.5% primary end point event rate in the placebo group, with 80% power to detect a 25% reduction in the relative risk of the varespladib group, necessitating the adjudication of 385 primary end point events.
assumed_rrr.note: Assumed placebo event rate 8.5% at 16 weeks.

power.quote: The trial was designed to enroll 6500 patients, assuming an 8.5% primary end point event rate in the placebo group, with 80% power to detect a 25% reduction in the relative risk of the varespladib group, necessitating the adjudication of 385 primary end point events.

alpha.quote: Significance testing was performed using 2-sided tests (α = .05) using SAS version 9.2 (SAS Institute).
alpha.note: Quote via WebFetch of JAMA full text.

stopped_early.quote: On March 9, 2012, at the prespecified interim analysis, when 212 primary outcomes had been recorded in 5012 randomized patients, the independent data and safety monitoring board recommended termination of the trial for futility according to predetermined criteria.
stopped_early.note: Stopped for futility (abstract adds 'and possible harm') at 212/385 = 55% of planned events; interim futility analysis prespecified at ~50% of events. Final adjudicated primary events 245 (136+109) because events up to 16 weeks after stop were counted. Anthera release (S5, 2012-03-09): 'due to a lack efficacy that could not be reasonably overcome in the remainder of the trial.' Registry whyStopped: 'Lack of efficacy'.

baseline.quote: At randomization, mean LDL-C was 105 mg/dL and HDL-C was 43 mg/dL.
baseline.note: Mean, via WebFetch of JAMA full text.

baseline.quote: Median (IQR) CRP was 10.4 (4.0-28.7) mg/L in the placebo group and 11.4 (4.5-33.0) mg/L in the varespladib group
baseline.note: Placebo median 10.4; varespladib 11.4 (acute phase, within 96 h of ACS).
NOT FOUND: no baseline sPLA2 reported in the JAMA paper. 'Patients were not selected for randomization on the basis of their underlying sPLA2 concentration or activity.'

biomarker_effects.note: NOT FOUND. JAMA paper reports no on-treatment sPLA2 data; Anthera's interim biomarker analysis (S4, 2011-04-18; S6 10-K) says only that varespladib 'met the pre-specified criteria' on sPLA2, LDL-C, CRP, IL-6, without numbers.

biomarker_effects.quote: Between randomization and week 16 of the study, LDL-C decreased by 28.8% in the varespladib group and 25.1% in the placebo group (P = .008).
biomarker_effects.note: Placebo-adjusted difference derived (28.8-25.1). Week-16 mean LDL-C 69.1 vs 73.8 mg/dL.

biomarker_effects.quote: Between randomization and week 16, CRP decreased by 85.0% in the varespladib group and 82.1% in the placebo group (P = .008).
biomarker_effects.note: Derived difference. Same P value (.008) as LDL-C reported - check against original.

biomarker_effects.quote: Respective 8-week median reductions in sPLA(2)-IIA levels were 82.4% and 15.6% (p < 0.0001)
biomarker_effects.note: Within-group varespladib -82.4% vs placebo -15.6%; difference derived. At 24 weeks: 78.5% vs 6.4%. FRANCIS: 625 ACS patients, varespladib 500 mg qd + atorvastatin 80 mg.

biomarker_effects.quote: After 8 weeks (primary efficacy end point), varespladib/atorvastatin reduced mean LDL-C levels from baseline by 49.6% compared with 43.4% with placebo/atorvastatin (p = 0.002).
and hsCRP levels were lowered by 75.0% and 71.0% (p = 0.097)
biomarker_effects.note: Not significant at 8 weeks; at 24 weeks 79.8% vs 77.0% (p=0.02). FRANCIS MACE at 6 months 7.3% vs 7.7%.

biomarker_effects.quote: Mean sPLA(2)-IIA concentration fell by 86.7%, from 157 pmol/L to 21 [corrected] pmol/L, in the overall active treatment group, and by 4.8%, from 157 pmol/L to 143 [corrected] pmol/L, in the placebo group (p<0.0001 treatment vs placebo).
biomarker_effects.note: Stable CHD, n=393, twice-daily dosing 50-500 mg; dose-dependent 69.2% (50 mg) to 95.8% (500 mg). Baseline sPLA2-IIA 157 pmol/L. Difference derived.

hr.quote: The primary end point occurred in 136 patients (6.1%) treated with varespladib compared with 109 patients (5.1%) treated with placebo (hazard ratio [HR], 1.25; 95% CI, 0.97-1.61; log-rank P = .08).

safety_signals.quote: Varespladib was associated with a greater risk of MI (78 [3.4%] vs 47 [2.2%]; HR, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.16-2.39; log-rank P = .005).

The composite secondary end point of cardiovascular mortality, MI, and stroke was observed in 107 patients (4.6%) in the varespladib group and 79 patients (3.8%) in the placebo group (HR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.02-1.82; P = .04).
There was an excess of alanine transaminase elevations more than 3 times the upper limit of normal during the treatment phase with varespladib (38 patients) compared with placebo (6 patients).
safety_signals.note: Via WebFetch of JAMA full text.

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization of PLA2G2A rs11573156 (lowers sPLA2-IIA mass 38-44% per allele) found no protection from major vascular events; genetic estimate differs from observational association
genetics.effect: OR per C allele 1.02 (0.98-1.06) general population; 0.96 (0.90-1.03) ACS cohorts; IV OR per 1-log lower sPLA2-IIA 1.04 (0.96-1.13) vs observational 0.69 (0.61-0.79)
genetics.quote: Reducing sPLA2-IIA mass is unlikely to be a useful therapeutic goal for preventing cardiovascular events.
genetics.note: Holmes et al., JACC 2013 (online 2013-07-31): after VISTA-16 readout (2012-03-09). Caveat: rs11573156 lowers sPLA2 enzyme activity only 3-23% per allele, and varespladib also inhibits groups V and X.

genetics.finding: Modified MR for sPLA2-V (PLA2G5 expression SNP rs525380) found no association with CHD
genetics.effect: OR for CHD per A allele 1.02 (0.99-1.04); no effect on sPLA2 activity (0.4%)
genetics.quote: The evidence does not support a causal role for sPLA2-V in CHD.
genetics.note: Holmes et al., Circ Cardiovasc Genet 2014; post-readout. Weak instrument (no effect on measured sPLA2 activity).

consensus_explanation.summary: Varespladib robustly lowered sPLA2-IIA concentration in phase 2 (~82-87%) but in VISTA-16 did not reduce, and probably increased, recurrent events (primary HR 1.25, MI HR 1.66); the trial was stopped for futility at the first interim. The field's explanation is that sPLA2-IIA is not causal for atherosclerotic events: the subsequent PLA2G2A Mendelian randomization (Holmes 2013, JACC) showed genetically lower sPLA2-IIA mass gives no protection, with the authors concluding that lowering sPLA2-IIA is not a useful therapeutic goal; an sPLA2-V MR (2014) was also null. The observed MI excess suggests possible drug-specific (off-target or broad sPLA2 isoform) harm, which remains unexplained. Phase 2 relied on biomarker surrogates (sPLA2, LDL-C, CRP) and small, short trials; FRANCIS showed no MACE signal (7.3% vs 7.7%). No human genetic validation of sPLA2 was found before the readout.

pre_readout.note: Readout = Anthera press release 2012-03-09 (S5), DSMB stop for lack of efficacy. Efficacy numbers (HR, MI harm) appeared only in JAMA 2013-11-18.
available_before_readout: Registry record (S3, first posted 2010-05-25): primary end point, eligibility
Design: up to 6,500 patients and minimum 385 primary events (S4 Anthera press release 2011-04-18); design paper (S2, Cardiovasc Drugs Ther, online ~2011-11-24; abstract free: 'Up to 6,500 patients')
Interim biomarker analysis 'met the pre-specified criteria' - no numbers (S4, 2011-04-18)
Phase 2 FRANCIS-ACS: sPLA2-IIA -82.4% vs -15.6% at 8 wk; LDL-C -49.6% vs -43.4%; no MACE difference 7.3% vs 7.7% (S8, JACC 2010-09-28)
Genetics: NONE FOUND before readout supporting or refuting PLA2G2A causality
only_after_readout: Power 80% / 25% RRR / 8.5% placebo event rate assumption (S1 JAMA 2013-11-18; not in the free design abstract or press releases reviewed)
Results: HR 1.25 (0.97-1.61), 136 vs 109 events, MI HR 1.66, interim at 212 events (S1, 2013-11-18)
Genetics: Holmes 2013 PLA2G2A MR (S9, 2013-07-31); Holmes 2014 sPLA2-V (S10, 2014-02-21)

access_summary.note: Counted by best free access. Open full text (JAMA S1 via WebFetch; jamanetwork blocks curl and shows a bot check in a browser): N, treatment duration, planned events, RRR, power, alpha, HR, CI x2, p, events x2, interim events (212), MI HR. HR/CI/p/events/212/MI HR are also in the free abstract; planned events 385 also in a press release (S4). Abstract only: FRANCIS sPLA2 (S8), PLASMA sPLA2 (S7). Not found: on-treatment sPLA2 reduction in VISTA-16. If JAMA full text is treated as not accessible, power/RRR/alpha become paywalled-only.

open_questions: On-treatment sPLA2 reduction in VISTA-16: NOT FOUND in JAMA paper, Anthera press releases (2011-04-18, 2012-03-09) or FY2011 10-K (interim biomarker analysis described only as meeting pre-specified criteria). Phase 2 FRANCIS-ACS (-82.4% at 8 wk) is the best available proxy.
N randomized: JAMA 5145 vs ClinicalTrials.gov enrollment 5189 (ACTUAL). Unresolved (possibly enrolled vs randomized, or registry not finalized; registry last updated 2012-10).

outcome_label set to 'failure' because the DSMB stopped the trial for futility (press release: 'lack of efficacy'); however the JAMA abstract says 'futility and possible harm' and MI was significantly increased (HR 1.66), so 'stopped_harm' is arguable.
Median follow-up NOT FOUND; stored the planned 16-week treatment duration instead.
JAMA reports P = .008 for both the LDL-C and the CRP between-group differences at 16 weeks (as relayed by WebFetch); not independently re-checked against the PDF.

JAMA full-text access: readable through WebFetch without login, but curl gets 403 and the browser shows a Cloudflare bot check. Europe PMC: not open access, no PMC copy. Full-text quotes were relayed by WebFetch's extraction model.

Design paper (S2) full text not read (Springer, paywalled); unknown whether it already stated 385 events / 80% power / 25% RRR before readout. The 385-event target was public via press release S4 (2011-04-18).
No pre-2012 PLA2G2A genetic study on CHD outcomes was identified; earlier PLA2G2A studies of sPLA2-IIA levels may exist but were not searched in depth.
FRANCIS JACC online-first date not confirmed; 2010-09-28 is the issue date (PubMed entry 2010-09-25).
